title: Project structure
text: Hello, I am Gagan N, USN 24BTRBT013, and this is the live demonstration of my project, Secure Peer-to-Peer Communication between Enterprise Corda Nodes. Everything you see here is running live on my laptop. First, here is the project structure: the contracts module with my state and contract, the workflows module with my flows, the crypto helper and the trust policy, and the RPC demo client.

title: Running the tests (gradlew test)
text: Next, I run the tests. Gradle runs the fifteen contract tests live now. The seven MockNetwork flow tests were run in full just before this recording, so Gradle reports them as up to date. The summary shows all twenty-two tests passing, including the privacy, integrity, trust policy and ciphertext tests.

title: Starting the 4 Corda nodes (Notary, EnterpriseA, EnterpriseB, EnterpriseC)
text: Now I start the four Corda nodes: the notary, EnterpriseA, EnterpriseB and EnterpriseC. Each node runs headless as its own Java process, with its own P2P and RPC ports, and my script waits for the started up line in each node's log. Starting a Corda node takes around a minute, because it loads the CorDapps, opens its vault database, starts the Artemis message broker and registers with the network map. While they start, remember my trust policy: EnterpriseA trusts only EnterpriseB, so EnterpriseC will be rejected later.

title: Network map
text: All four nodes are up. Here is the network map as EnterpriseA sees it: three enterprise nodes and the non-validating notary, each with its X.500 name and its P2P address.

title: Certificates (keytool summary for EnterpriseA)
text: Now the certificates. I run keytool on EnterpriseA's three keystores. The TLS key store holds a chain of four certificates, from the node's TLS certificate through the node CA and the Doorman CA up to the Corda root CA. The identity key is Ed25519, and the trust store contains only the root CA.

title: TLS handshake (openssl s_client -tls1_2 against EnterpriseA:10005)
text: Next, I test the P2P port with openssl, using TLS 1.2 and no client certificate. The server presents EnterpriseA's certificate and asks for a client certificate. Because I have none, the handshake fails with alert forty. With a real network certificate the handshake completes, and TLS 1.3 is refused. So mutual TLS is enforced.

title: Sending encrypted messages EnterpriseA -> EnterpriseB
text: Now the main part. EnterpriseA sends three confidential messages to EnterpriseB, and B sends one invoice back. For each message, the flow runs an X25519 key exchange over the session, encrypts the body with AES-256-GCM, collects both signatures and notarises the transaction. The table shows that only ciphertext is stored on the ledger.

title: Acknowledge + decrypt on EnterpriseB with the integrity check
text: Next, each receiver acknowledges its messages. Before acknowledging, the receiver decrypts the message and verifies its SHA-256 hash. Then EnterpriseB reads the purchase order. The decrypted body appears, and the hash on the ledger matches the hash of the decrypted text, so the integrity check passes.

title: Privacy proof: EnterpriseC vault = 0
text: This is the privacy proof. EnterpriseA and EnterpriseB each have eight message states: the consumed SENT states plus the ACKNOWLEDGED ones. EnterpriseC has zero. It was never a participant, so it never received any of these transactions.

title: Untrusted peer: EnterpriseC -> EnterpriseA
text: Now EnterpriseC tries to send a message to EnterpriseA. EnterpriseA's responder flow checks its trusted peers list, does not find EnterpriseC, and throws the exception: Untrusted peer. No state is created.

title: P2P latency: PingPeerFlow x20 (EnterpriseA -> EnterpriseB)
text: Next, I measure the P2P latency. PingPeerFlow does twenty send and receive round trips from EnterpriseA to EnterpriseB over the TLS link, and the table shows the average, minimum, maximum and median latency in milliseconds.

title: Stopping the nodes
text: To finish, I stop all four nodes. That completes my live demonstration of secure, private and verifiable peer-to-peer messaging between enterprise Corda nodes. Thank you for watching.
